turns.content: In (1R,3R,4R,6S)-1,3,4-trimethyl-7-oxabicyclo[4.1.0]heptane, identify the two epoxide carbons and compare their steric substitution.
From that comparison, determine which epoxide carbon is less hindered and explain the local structural reason.
For reaction with Me2CuLi, apply the organocuprate epoxide-opening rule to select the attacked carbon and state the stereochemical mode of attack.
After workup, identify which original C-O bond has broken, which carbon received the new methyl group, and which carbon now bears the alcohol.
Map the original ring atoms onto the product numbering used for a substituted cyclohexan-1-ol.
At the attacked carbon, determine the product-side CIP priority order and assign its absolute configuration rather than transferring the starting label mechanically.
Track the configurations of the remaining stereocenters under the product numbering.
Verify independently that methyl attack occurred at original C6 while oxygen remained attached to original C1.
Reconcile backside attack at C6 with the product-side R/S assignment, taking account of the changed substituent priorities.
Give the complete stereochemical name of the ring-opened alcohol and summarize the attack-site and atom-mapping argument.
